title: Causal odd-syndrome/time-boundary handoff matrix
authorization: Follow-up to the closed-censored J6 pilot. This registration addresses its localized public-interface domain gap only; it neither repairs nor reanalyzes J6.

program_alignment.central_question: Can a causal spacetime scheduler hand a valid odd instantaneous noisy syndrome to the spatial D4 decoder without inventing a spatial correction, reading future records, or exposing private truth?
program_alignment.epistemic_role: Prerequisite implementation gate for a future, separately registered replacement pilot
program_alignment.upstream_dependency: J6 production closed censored after 272 histories and 2,176 unconditional rows; the static periodic spatial decoder rejected valid odd instantaneous measured syndromes.
program_alignment.downstream_consumer: Only a new J6B pilot registration after every J6A gate passes.
program_alignment.information_value: Distinguishes a causal admissible temporal-boundary representation from a hidden-truth completion or a post-hoc J6 data repair.

question: For a committed causal prefix whose instantaneous flux snapshot has odd parity solely because of readout noise, can the schedule emit a typed, digest-bound temporal-boundary handoff that makes the augmented decoder request admissible while preserving causal and truth-free behavior?
smallest_intended_claim: A passing matrix establishes only that the registered public handoff interface is deterministic, causal, parity-accounted, and fail-closed on fixed fixtures. It does not establish logical performance, schedule advantage, a noise model, or a fault-tolerance result.
non_goals: Do not modify, rescore, bootstrap, filter, or reinterpret any J6 production row.
Do not generate a stochastic history, run a schedule arm, or compare schedule/mode risk.
Do not pair an odd spatial endpoint to an arbitrary hidden or future spatial vertex.
Do not claim that the temporal-boundary bookkeeping is a microscopic D(S3) circuit derivation.

interface_contract.public_input: The scheduler consumes only the committed causal prefix, its visible syndrome detector/readout rows, declared decision round, mode, and existing public request digest.
interface_contract.public_output: A versioned handoff object containing only a sorted odd-endpoint list, their decision-time temporal-boundary labels, the committed round, and a canonical digest bound to the causal prefix and request.
interface_contract.spatial_semantics: The spatial decoder receives an augmented matching request. Each handed endpoint is paired to an explicit temporal boundary rather than to a fabricated spatial endpoint; the handoff itself is a defer/ledger action, not a physical spatial correction.
interface_contract.resolution_semantics: A later causal detector/readout update may reconcile, supersede, or retain a temporal-boundary token only through a new digest-bound request; current requests are immutable.
interface_contract.private_boundary: Hidden support, physical fault chain, post-action relation, logical sector, residual truth, future readout, and future detector events are unavailable to handoff construction and decoding.

fixed_fixture_matrix.required_result: No temporal-boundary token; existing spatial request/action remains byte-identical.

fixed_fixture_matrix.case: one visible odd endpoint at the decision round
fixed_fixture_matrix.required_result: One typed temporal-boundary token; augmented endpoint parity is even; no fabricated spatial correction is emitted.

fixed_fixture_matrix.case: odd snapshot followed by a causal visible partner/change
fixed_fixture_matrix.required_result: Later request reconciles through a new token/action digest without mutating the earlier request.

fixed_fixture_matrix.case: odd snapshot remains through the terminal available prefix
fixed_fixture_matrix.required_result: Token remains explicitly unresolved and the public action is defer/fail-closed, never truth-completed.

fixed_fixture_matrix.case: append future visible rounds after an earlier decision
fixed_fixture_matrix.required_result: Earlier handoff object, request digest, and action are unchanged.
All public handoff and decoder outputs are unchanged.

fixed_fixture_matrix.case: repeat a fixture and relabel the periodic vertex consistently
fixed_fixture_matrix.required_result: Replay is bit-identical and the public object is equivariant under the declared relabelling.

fixed_fixture_matrix.case: missing prefix binding, bad round, duplicate endpoint, or unknown token
fixed_fixture_matrix.required_result: Reject before decoder execution and preserve the unconditional caller denominator semantics.

acceptance_gates: All eight fixed fixtures pass with no hidden/future field in any public request, digest, or action.
Every augmented request has even matching parity, while its physical spatial correction boundary equals only the non-handoff spatial component.
Odd endpoints are represented only by explicit temporal-boundary tokens and are never silently dropped or matched to an invented spatial vertex.
Earlier outputs remain invariant under future extension and private-sidecar changes; replay is bit-identical.
Malformed, stale, or duplicate handoffs fail closed before spatial decoding and emit a machine-readable reason.
The existing J6 raw rows and analysis SHA-256 values remain unchanged.
stop_rule: Registration creates no fixture result or code change. On execution, run exactly the eight fixed deterministic fixtures. Stop on the first provenance, causality, parity-accounting, anti-leakage, replay, or malformed-input failure; write a censored result and keep J6B blocked. A pass permits only J6B registration, never reuse or amendment of J6.

follow_on.release_condition: Every J6A acceptance gate passes in its durable machine-readable result.

pre_execution_source_scope_correction.observed_failure: The current D4SpatialCommitRequestV1.from_dict rejects a one-vertex odd public syndrome with ValueError: periodic D4 flux syndrome must have even cardinality. The scheduler's E1PolicyDecoder invokes typed_record_to_commit_request and decode_flux_action on that path before a handoff can exist.
pre_execution_source_scope_correction.registration_defect: The original allowed-file set omitted scripts/e1_schedule_integration.py, the public scheduler entry point needed to route a causal temporal-boundary handoff; a helper-only test would not satisfy the registered end-to-end claim.
pre_execution_source_scope_correction.correction: Add only the scheduler adapter and its existing test file to the allowed implementation scope. Keep the same eight fixtures, physical model, zero-history/evaluation/bootstrap budget, no external dependency, unconditional denominator, and no J6 row modifications.
pre_execution_source_scope_correction.release_gate: The eight fixtures must exercise the actual scheduler-to-spatial public handoff path, not only a direct helper; odd records must not be silently converted to an even spatial syndrome. J6B remains blocked until this path and every original acceptance gate pass.

execution_result.interpretation: Digest-bound, all-defer temporal-boundary handoff is a structural public-interface pass only. No production histories, risk estimates, or schedule comparisons; persistent odd snapshots remain unresolved and fail closed.
